title: Searchable assignee picker
prompt: Replace the placeholder in `TaskAssigneeField` with a proper assignee picker: a button that opens a searchable popover listing project members from `useMembersQuery`. Show loading, error, and no-results states. Each member shows an avatar (initials fallback), name, and email, and the selected member gets a check mark. The parent controls the value, which can be cleared back to unassigned (`undefined`). We'll reuse this picker for choosing reviewers later, so make it reusable.

criteria.text: A generic picker family (src/components/ui, outside the tasks/members features) knows only UI: no useMembersQuery, Member type, member fetching, or task policy. The consumer (TaskAssigneeField) runs the query and composes the family; member-specific anatomy lives in a record part in the feature (e.g. MemberComboboxItem). The family is reusable for reviewers without edits.

The consumer reads the members query and maps the members inside the list part into item parts (`members.data?.map((member) => <MemberComboboxItem key={member.id} member={member} />)`), and the avatar/name/email/check anatomy is written once in that record item part. Enumeration through a render-function child (`{(member) => ...}`), a Collection part, `items` passed to the root, or a closed component that hardcodes the anatomy inside the generic family are fails.

Roots hold only shared state (value/onValueChange/open). Neither the generic root nor any member wrapper takes items, loading/error flags, placeholder or other copy, aria-*, or className: aria-labelledby and width go on the trigger part, the placeholder on the value part, the clear option's text as its children. A closed `<MemberCombobox aria-labelledby className projectId value onValueChange unselectedLabel />` is a fail.

Loading, error, and empty are focused child parts placed inside the list and rendered from the consumer's query state (cmdk's Empty may self-gate on search results); they do not render alongside stale results incorrectly, and no root flag gates them.

The picker supports a controlled value where `undefined` (unassigned) is a valid controlled value: controlledness is determined by prop presence (e.g. `'value' in props` / hasOwnProperty) or the component is controlled-only by design with value typed `string | undefined` and onValueChange required; clearing to undefined does not flip it into uncontrolled mode. A clear/unassign affordance exists.

Each option establishes its identity once (value/id on the item boundary); nested parts such as the check indicator derive selection from that boundary rather than receiving repeated `selected`/`index` props computed by the consumer.

Trigger, content, input, list, and item parts accept their primitive's props (Button/PopoverContent/CommandInput/CommandItem); no triggerProps/contentProps/itemProps bags; placeholder and labels are passed to the part that renders them.

Builds on the existing Popover and Command primitives, preserving their keyboard/ARIA behavior (cmdk filtering is disabled or reconciled with server search via shouldFilter={false} or equivalent); className merged last; required bindings applied after spreads.

Optional JSX uses `&&` only with boolean conditions; nullable values are compared explicitly (`src != null &&`, `items.length > 0 &&`) and no `cond ? <X/> : null`; no routine manual memoization (React Compiler enabled); no module-global store; state machinery proportional to need (no unrequested uncontrolled mode).
TaskAssigneeField uses the picker with the existing props contract, search is wired to useMembersQuery, and the code typechecks.
